Standard: The occupant is kept in position with respect to support of the seating system under both inertial and applied loads (e.g., aerodynamic pressure). The restraint system prevents "submarining" or translation of the pelvis under the lap belt. The shoulders are restrained to align the thoracic and lumbar spine with the seat back. The restraint system ensures that ejection posture is maintained up to seat occupant separation. Torso displacement, as measured from the base of the neck (cervical vertebrae C7/T1) to the back tangent line, is less than 3.0 inches. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Test.
(1) Lab test: Subsystem dynamic load tests verify restraint mechanical integrity, seat back alignment, and torso displacement.
(2) Lab test: System-level dynamic ejection sled tests verify full escape system restraint capability.
